title: Jesus Addresses the Multitude
summary: Jesus looks around at the multitude. He says his time is at hand, tells them they are weak and cannot understand all his words, directs them to go home and prepare for the morrow, and says he will go to the Father and show himself to the lost tribes of Israel.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus looks around at the multitude and says his time is at hand.
Jesus says the multitude is weak and cannot understand all his words at this time.
Jesus tells them to go home, ponder his words, ask the Father in his name for understanding, and prepare their minds for the morrow. He says he will come to them again.
Jesus says he will go to the Father and show himself to the lost tribes of Israel.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus faces the gathered multitude while addressing them.
unspecified_visual_details: The gathering place and its surroundings.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, my time is at hand.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus

spoken_dialogue.text: I perceive that ye are weak,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus

spoken_dialogue.text: Therefore, go ye unto your homes, and ponder upon the things which I have said,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus

spoken_dialogue.text: But now I go unto the Father, and also to show myself unto the lost tribes of Israel,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Jesus speaks of going to the Father and showing himself to the lost tribes; neither event occurs within these verses.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Jesus departing or appearing to the lost tribes in this scene.
Do not depict the Father or the lost tribes as physically present.
Do not assign a specific location or invented identities to members of the multitude.

title: Jesus Addresses the Tearful Multitude
summary: Jesus sees the multitude in tears, looking steadfastly at him as if asking him to stay longer. He expresses compassion, invites the sick and afflicted to come to him, and says he will heal them.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus looks around and sees the multitude in tears, looking steadfastly at him as if they would ask him to stay longer.
Jesus says he is filled with compassion toward them.
Jesus invites those who are sick or afflicted to come to him and says he will heal them.
Jesus says he perceives their desire to see what he has done for their brethren at Jerusalem and that their faith is sufficient for him to heal them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The multitude is gathered near Jesus.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearances of individuals in the multitude.
The appearance of any particular ailment.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, my bowels are filled with compassion towards you.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus

spoken_dialogue.text: Bring them hither and I will heal them, for I have compassion upon you; my bowels are filled with mercy.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus

spoken_dialogue.text: For I perceive that ye desire that I should show unto you what I have done unto your brethren at Jerusalem, for I see that your faith is sufficient that I should heal you.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus

doctrinal_or_story_notes: What Jesus did for their brethren at Jerusalem is mentioned in speech, not shown here.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict events at Jerusalem.
Do not depict a healing as already occurring in this scene.
Do not depict the multitude explicitly asking Jesus to stay; the verse describes their looks as if they would ask.

title: The Sick Are Healed
summary: The multitude brings the sick and afflicted to Jesus, and he heals them as they are brought forth.

explicit_facts.text: The multitude brings the sick, afflicted, lame, blind, dumb, and others afflicted in any manner to Jesus, and he heals each as they are brought to him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People bring others forward to Jesus in succession.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific diagnoses, healing gestures, and visual effects.

narration.text: and he did heal them every one

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a particular healing method or visible supernatural effect.

title: The Multitude Worships
summary: Those who were healed and those who were whole bow down and worship Jesus; many kiss his feet and bathe them with tears.

explicit_facts.text: The healed and the whole bow down at Jesus's feet and worship him; as many as can reach him kiss his feet and bathe them with tears.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The multitude gathers around Jesus as people bow and approach his feet.
unspecified_visual_details: How many people can reach Jesus and the exact arrangement of the crowd.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict additional speech or actions.

title: The Children Are Brought
summary: Jesus commands that the little children be brought. They are set on the ground around him, and the multitude makes way until they have all been brought.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus commands that the little children be brought.
The children are brought and set down on the ground around Jesus, who stands in their midst; the multitude makes way until they have all been brought.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Adults in the multitude carry or guide children toward the place around Jesus.
unspecified_visual_details: The children's ages, clothing, and individual appearances.
prohibited_inventions: Do not assign names or relationships to the children or the people bringing them.

title: The Multitude Kneels
summary: With Jesus standing among the children, he commands the multitude to kneel. They kneel, and Jesus groans within himself and speaks to the Father about the wickedness of the people of the house of Israel.

explicit_facts.text: After all the children are brought, Jesus stands in their midst and commands the multitude to kneel on the ground.
The multitude kneels; Jesus groans within himself and says he is troubled because of the wickedness of the people of the house of Israel.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The multitude kneels around Jesus and the children.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact posture or expression accompanying Jesus's inward groan.

spoken_dialogue.text: Father, I am troubled because of the wickedness of the people of the house of Israel.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The wickedness of the people of the house of Israel is mentioned, not depicted.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the people of the house of Israel or invent a visible cause for Jesus's distress.

title: Jesus Prays
summary: After speaking, Jesus kneels upon the earth and prays to the Father. The multitude hears him and bears record.

explicit_facts.text: After speaking, Jesus kneels upon the earth and prays to the Father. What he prays cannot be written. The multitude hears him and bears record.
In its record, the multitude says it saw and heard Jesus speak to the Father and calls those things great and marvelous.
The multitude says the things it saw and heard Jesus speak cannot be spoken or written, and that joy filled its souls when it heard him pray for them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The multitude is close enough to hear Jesus pray.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearances and positions of individual members of the multitude.

narration.text: he himself also knelt upon the earth
the multitude did bear record who heard him.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verses 16–17 give the multitude's testimony, not additional visible events to stage.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent words for the unrecorded prayer.
Do not depict the Father; no appearance is described.
Do not stage the multitude's testimony as a separate present-tense event.

title: The Multitude Is Overcome
summary: After Jesus finishes praying and rises, the multitude is overcome by joy. Jesus tells them to arise.

explicit_facts.text: After Jesus finishes praying to the Father, he rises, and the multitude is overcome by great joy.
Jesus speaks to the multitude and bids them arise.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The multitude is still gathered with Jesus and the children.
unspecified_visual_details: How the multitude shows that they are overcome.

narration.text: so great was the joy of the multitude that they were overcome

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a particular physical response to being overcome.

title: Jesus Blesses the Children
summary: The multitude rises. Jesus blesses them for their faith and says his joy is full; he weeps, takes the children one by one, blesses them, and prays for them. He weeps again afterward.

explicit_facts.text: The multitude rises from the earth; Jesus says they are blessed because of their faith and that his joy is full.
Jesus weeps, takes the little children one by one, blesses them, and prays to the Father for them.
After doing this, Jesus weeps again.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus attends to each child in turn while the multitude is present.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific words of each blessing and prayer.

spoken_dialogue.text: Blessed are ye because of your faith.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

spoken_dialogue.text: And now behold, my joy is full.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: he took their little children, one by one, and blessed them

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The text does not provide the words of the individual blessings or prayers.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the words of the blessings or prayers.

title: Angels Minister to the Children
summary: Jesus tells the multitude to behold the children. They look toward heaven and see it open, angels descending as it were in the midst of fire, encircling the children amid fire and ministering to them. The multitude sees and hears this and bears record.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus speaks to the multitude and tells them to behold their little ones.
The multitude looks toward heaven and sees the heavens open and angels descending as it were in the midst of fire; the angels encircle the children amid fire and minister to them.
The multitude sees, hears, and bears record; about two thousand five hundred souls, consisting of men, women, and children, witness it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The children are at the center of the angels' encircling ministry.
unspecified_visual_details: The angels' individual appearances and number.
The appearance and color of the fire.

narration.text: the angels did minister unto them

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The angels and the opening heavens are explicitly seen in the account and may be depicted.
“As it were in the midst of fire” describes how the angels are seen; do not add destructive effects.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent individual angel names, biographies, or dialogue.
Do not depict the Father, who is not described as appearing.
